organizations.normalization_notes: Historical employer name is retained; student status and employment are separate relationships. The cited sources do not establish which Maryland campus employed Dozer.
Earlier government service is distinct from later OSS/COI work and from the last civilian employer.

affiliations.date_precision: The obituary says Dozer joined Maryland's faculty in 1937 and returned to government intelligence service in 1942; the June 1941 journal byline independently places him at the university. Exact departure and OSS-entry dates are not established.
affiliations.research_notes: Published as the last civilian employer before 1942 government intelligence service, not as an explicitly immediate predecessor to OSS. The specific intelligence office and formal OSS entry require Box 198.

affiliations.date_precision: The obituary names 1936 State Department archivist service and says he joined Maryland's faculty the following year; exact appointment dates are unknown.
affiliations.research_notes: Earlier government assignment documented by one inspected obituary. It is not the last civilian employer and is not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Donald M Dozer is linked with high confidence to historian Donald Marquand Dozer, who later served in wartime government intelligence.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index names Donald M Dozer in the OSS personnel series. A June 1941 contemporaneous byline expands the distinctive middle initial to Marquand and places him at Maryland; the Washington Post obituary identifies Donald M Dozer with that faculty career and 1942 government intelligence service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: distinctive indexed first name, surname, and middle initial; independently documented full middle name; prewar Maryland and 1942 intelligence chronology fit the index. Box 198 has not been examined, so identity is not marked confirmed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The magazine is dated June 1941; the obituary dates the faculty-to-government transition to 1942. The exact OSS-entry date is not documented by the inspected sources.
claims.match_notes: Do not identify the 1942 government office more precisely from the obituary's generic 'intelligence official' wording, or import an uninspected university memorial from a search snippet.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA prints Donald M Dozer in Box 198; a contemporary June 1941 magazine byline expands the distinctive name to Donald Marquand Dozer at the University of Maryland; the Washington Post obituary links Donald M Dozer's Maryland faculty appointment to 1942 government intelligence service. Box 198 is unopened.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 198 for precise COI/OSS entry, Maryland departure date, and any intervening 1942 government assignment; do not call Maryland the immediate pre-OSS employer without that chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA prints Alexis N Dragnich in Box 198. Vanderbilt University's obituary identifies an Alex N. Dragnich who completed Berkeley doctoral work in 1942 and served as an OSS foreign-affairs analyst. The unusual surname, middle initial, and OSS context make this a plausible candidate, but the first names differ and no direct Alex/Alexis bridge or Box 198 identifier has been inspected. Student status is not employment.
person_updates.next_action: Inspect Box 198 and a contemporaneous OSS personnel record for the indexed Alexis N Dragnich; compare birth or education data with the Vanderbilt Alex N Dragnich before accepting the candidate. Do not assign Berkeley or later Vanderbilt as a pre-OSS employer from this source.
